newsitem.title: UK: Oil price slips again as stock cover builds.
newsitem.headline: Oil price slips again as stock cover builds.

text.p: World oil prices slipped a little further on Monday adding to the heavy losses posted since crude's bull run failed at the end of January.
Bellwether London futures for North Sea March Brent fell 14 cents to $20.36 a barrel.
Dealers said they were bracing for the possibility that the market might ease further as winter demand peters out and refiners close capacity for maintenance.
"We might see a bounce back in the short term, but beyond that I'd say supplies look sufficient to push this market lower," said a London-based trader.
Analysts said oil company stock cover, stretched to the limit for several months last year, was quickly returning to comfortable levels.

"With company stock cover expected to come much closer to normal levels during the current quarter, it is small wonder that oil prices have been weakening," said London consultancy the Centre for Global Energy Studies (CGES).
First quarter oil markets, which have seen stock draws of 1.7 million barrels a day (bpd) in previous years, were heading for zero stock change this year, the CGES said.
"With Iraq's limited oil sales in full swing, OPEC may finally be producing just too much oil for comfort."

Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries member Iraq has returned to customers to place extra cargoes in an effort to accrue the $1 billion worth of sales it is permitted by mid-March under the United Nations oil-for-food exchange.
OPEC pumped 26.64 million bpd in January in Iraq's first full month of exports under the U.N. plan and has added 600,000 bpd in two months.
